Key findings: Speed at impact 52-58 kmph for Pulsar, victim's helmet prevented skull fracture but sustained significant impact, blood alcohol negative for both, vehicle damage consistent with collision dynamics, paint transfer confirmed. Accident reconstruction confirms primary fault of Pulsar rider. Formal report awaited. Preliminary findings included in case file for reference.; Reports Received: Preliminary FSL findings (verbal and email); Entry No.: CD-13; Entry Date and time: 18 November 2024, 12:00; Received final FSL Report No. FSL/DL/2024/PHY/8934 dated 18-11-2024. Complete forensic examination confirms all investigation findings. Report includes vehicle examination, helmet analysis, blood analysis, accident reconstruction, and CCTV correlation. All exhibits returned from FSL to Malkhana. FSL report made part of case file. Key conclusions: (1) Accident caused by overspeeding of Pulsar (52-58 kmph vs 40 kmph limit), (2) Victim had no contributory negligence, (3) Helmet saved victim from fatal head injury, (4) Both vehicles mechanically sound before accident.; Reports Received: FSL Report No. FSL/DL/2024/PHY/8934; Entry No.: CD-14; Entry Date and time: 22 November 2024, 10:00; Victim Rajesh Sharma discharged from hospital on 20-11-2024 after 36 days of treatment. Obtained final discharge summary and fitness certificate. Victim advised 3 months physiotherapy, follow-up in Ortho and Neuro OPD. Permanent disability assessment after 6 months. Recorded final statement of victim regarding expenses incurred (approximately ■4.2 lakhs medical expenses), loss of salary (3 months leave without pay), and ongoing treatment needs. Victim expresses desire for compensation and strict punishment to accused. Documents collected for Victim Compensation Scheme application.; Statements Recorded: Final victim statement; Documents Obtained: Discharge summary, Medical bills, Salary slips, Physiotherapy prescription; Entry No.: CD-15; Entry Date and time: 28 November 2024, 10:00; Investigation complete. All evidence collected, statements recorded, forensic reports received. Prima facie case well established against accused Amit Verma for offences under Section 281 BNS (Rash driving), Section 125 BNS (Act endangering life), Section 184 MV Act (Dangerous driving), and Section 134 MV Act (Failure to provide medical aid - accused did not actively assist victim though he was also injured, however the attempt to leave initially constitutes violation). Evidence list finalized - 15 exhibits. Case diary complete with 15 entries. All documents compiled and indexed in Annexures. Victim suffered grievous injuries requiring 36 days hospitalization and may have permanent disability. No contributory negligence by victim. Accused has no criminal history but his actions show disregard for traffic rules and public safety. Registered FIR No. 452/2024 under sections 281/125 BNS and 184/134 MV Act on complaint of Smt. Sunita Sharma, wife of victim. Arrested accused Amit Verma at 19:15 hours from spot. Witness statement:
Document ID: bc74e5bb-238e-4eb3-88f9-376e412e1e40
Statement date: 15 October 2024
Witness name: Mohammed Asif
Witness address: Police Lines, Rajinder Nagar, New Delhi
Recorded by: Inspector Suresh Chandra
Statement text: I, Mohammed Asif, Traffic Police Constable Badge No. 3342, posted at Karol
Bagh Traffic Circle, state that on 15.10.2024, I was on duty at Shankar Road T-point near St.
Stephen's Hospital from 4 PM to 8 PM. My duty was to manage traffic at this intersection. The traffic
signal at this T-point has been non-functional since 3 days and we are manually managing traffic
with hand signals. At approximately 6:20 PM, I was standing at the junction managing traffic flow. I
saw a red colored Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle coming from Shankar Road from Karol Bagh side at a
very high speed. I estimate the speed was above 60 kmph. I signaled the rider to slow down as
there was traffic at the junction, but he did not reduce speed. He was looking down at his mobile
phone which was mounted on the handlebar, possibly checking map or delivery details. The traffic
coming from Rajinder Nagar side had the right of way and vehicles were turning towards Old
Rajinder Nagar. One white Honda Activa scooter was taking a legal right turn from Rajinder Nagar
side towards Old Rajinder Nagar. When this Activa was in the middle of the turn, the red Pulsar
coming at high speed from Shankar Road side entered the junction against my hand signal which
indicated STOP for vehicles from his side, and directly collided with the right side of the Activa. The
impact was so severe that the Activa rider was thrown off the scooter and landed on the road about
10-12 feet away. The Pulsar rider also fell down but got up quickly. He tried to pick up his bike to
leave the spot. I immediately ran towards him and caught him. With the help of some public
persons, I made him sit on the footpath. I called the PCR on 100 number from my mobile at 18:21
hours. The PCR van arrived at about 18:30-31 hours. I also called for an ambulance from St.
Stephen's Hospital which is just opposite. The ambulance came within 5-7 minutes and took the
injured scooter rider to the hospital. I handed over the Pulsar rider to the PCR staff and also gave
my initial account to them. I can identify the accused person, he was wearing a red Zomato t-shirt.
The victim was wearing a helmet which probably saved his life. The accused was also wearing a
helmet. I am making this statement voluntarily and it contains true facts of what I witnessed.

One person was lying on the road near the divider, another person was getting up. I saw that a red motorcycle had crashed into a white Activa scooter.
